answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes of knowing (or should have known) that a death of an individual at the mine has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the accidents requiring this immediate notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained with an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the miner for 1 hour or longer. Specifically, each operator must make available an approved self-rescue device "which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer." This requirement can be met by: (a) a 1-hour SCSR; (b) an SCSR of not less than 10 minutes combined with a 1-hour canister; or (c) any other self-contained breathing apparatus approved by MSHA that provides protection for a period of 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available a self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: This can be satisfied by a 1-hour SCSR.
Or by an SCSR of not less than 10 minutes combined with a 1-hour canister.
claims.quote: (b) A SCSR of not less than 10 minutes and a 1-hour canister; or

claims.text: Or any other approved self-contained breathing apparatus providing protection for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: (c) Any other self-contained breathing apparatus which provides protection for a period of 1 hour or longer and which is approved for use by MSHA as a self-rescue device when used and maintained as prescribed by MSHA.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: An underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months.

claims.text: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. This training must be conducted in conditions that, as closely as practicable, duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 of the 40 hours must be given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training must duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable, and about 8 hours must be given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise at a mine is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a dose of 100% as defined by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air in an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan requirements. All chunks relate to Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) regulations (30 CFR) on respirable dust control plans, respiratory protection, and quality control plans for fuses—none address OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain OSHA trenching regulations (e.g., 29 CFR 1926) regarding trench depth requirements for protective systems like shoring or trench boxes. The chunks available only cover MSHA/CFR Title 30 mining regulations (shafts, hoisting buckets, ROPS, etc.), so I cannot answer this question from the given material.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about FAA certification requirements for pilots flying drones over mine sites. The chunks only cover MSHA regulations on mine hazard training, mine map certification by state-registered engineers/surveyors, and miner training records—none of which address drone operations or FAA requirements.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about EPA stormwater discharge permits for mine site runoff. The available chunks only cover diesel engine emission requirements (§57.5067) and permits for underwater mining operations near rivers, streams, or lakes (§75.1716 series), which are unrelated to stormwater discharge permitting.
